text:
Alex G: FYI – Support escalated a customer (C-172) with huge p95/p99 spikes on text-generation since ~05:30 UTC. They reported interactive app slowdowns. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~380ms; p99s are hitting 1.2s. Logs point to a change around 05:10.

Priya S: ugh, that aligns with the runtime rollout 3.9.2 we pushed at 05:05 that enabled FlashAttention by default and adjusted SDPA heuristics. I flagged that change for perf wins but didn't expect regressions on long sequences.

Jamal R: I'm pulling kernel selection traces now. Quick grep from runtime logs:
```
[05:09:58] model=gptq-4k seq_len=1024 kernel=flash_attn selected=true
[05:09:59] kernel_switch -> fallback=sdpa reason=timeout
[05:10:01] kv-cache-miss batch=1 latency=320ms
```
Looks like for some requests runtime initially picks flash_attn then falls back to SDPA (fallback path is expensive and causing tail latencies).

Sofia M: Is the fallback happening because flash kernel runs out of workspace or hits an OOM? Any alloc failures?

Jamal R: No explicit OOM. The fallback path is triggered by a compile-flag guard we added: when kernel_exec_time > threshold we probe SDPA as fallback. That probe path does extra copies. For seq_len > 512 and batch=1 we're seeing probe timeouts more often.

Rachel T: Support reproduced with a minimal curl. Repro steps from them:
1) POST /v1/generate with model=gptq-4k, prompt len ~700 tokens (seq_len ~900)
2) batch_size=1, temperature=0.7, max_tokens=512
3) p95 ~400ms, p99 ~1-1.3s (compared to ~120/250 before)

Alex G: Can you paste the exact curl they used? We should reproduce locally.

Rachel T: Here it is: `curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gptq-4k","input":"<~700-token-prompt>","max_tokens":512}'`

Jamal R: Running local microbench (on same machine family) with env toggles:
- baseline (v3.8.x, flashattn disabled): p95=130ms p99=260ms
- v3.9.2 default: p95=390ms p99=1.1s
- v3.9.2 with REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1: p95=135ms p99=270ms
So toggling off FlashAttention reproduces the improvement.

Priya S: OK this confirms the new defaults are the culprit. Two possible angles: immediate mitigation (disable at runtime for affected nodes or customers) and long-term fix (tune flash-attn / probe heuristics or revert compile flag).

Sofia M: For mitigation we can:
- set per-customer routing to a variant with flash disabled
- set runtime env REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 on affected pool (fast but coarse)
- change kernel probe timeout to be more conservative so fallback doesn't trigger for interactive workloads
Which do we prefer for fastest customer relief?

Alex G: Short-term: flip env on the Dedicated pools serving their tenant and on the canary nodes in hosted to restore tail latency. Priya, can you patch the canary config? Jamal, please run a regression matrix and share numbers. Sofia, coordinate with support to tell C-172 we're applying a hotfix.

Priya S: On it. I'm creating a canary override: in console -> runtime flags -> canary: `disable_flash_attention=true` for 10% of traffic to validate. I'll post changes and wait for metrics.

deploy-bot: Starting deploy for runtime-flags canary (change id=rlf-2026) at 05:42 UTC.

Jamal R: Running bench matrix now (seq lens 256/512/768/1024, batch 1..8) with both kernels. Initial numbers: flash wins for batch>=4 and seq<=512. For seq>512 and batch=1 flash has higher variance and probe timeouts cause fallback path cost > sdpa. I'll upload CSV to the perf bucket.

ops-bot: Canary rollout (rlf-2026) reached 10% at 05:45 UTC. Telemetry: p95 on canary dropped from 380ms to 140ms within 5m.

Rachel T: Verified with customer — they report interactive feel back to normal after 06:00 UTC. They see p95 ~150ms. They've accepted the temporary fix. :relieved:

Priya S: Next steps I propose:
- revert the default enablement of flash_attn in the next stable release (3.9.3) until we harden probe heuristics
- add guard to avoid probing flash_attn for seq_len>512 when batch_size <=2 (we saw that pattern)
- add a runtime metric for "kernel_probe_count" and "probe_fallback_cost" so we can alert earlier
- automations: console flag to disable flash per model or per-tenant (already partially in place)

Alex G: Agreed. Jamal can you own the probe heuristics change and benchmarking matrix (Jamal -> action). Priya will own the release revert and runtime metric (Priya -> action). Sofia to open incident ticket INC-4123 with timeline and customer comms; include perf CSV and logs. I'll own the postmortem and we should sync with research about kernel parameters.

Jamal R: I'll also run synthetic stress tests on A100 and H100 to ensure no hardware-specific regressions. ETA for a validated heuristics patch: 48 hours.

Priya S: Created PR to revert the default flag: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123 – includes instructions to cherry-pick to hotfix branch.

deploy-bot: Hotfix canary deploy started for runtime v3.9.3-hotfix at 07:10 UTC (deploy id=hot-331).

ops-bot: Hotfix deployed to affected pools at 07:22 UTC. Post-deploy checks: p95/p99 stabilized to pre-rollout baselines for the impacted customers.

Sofia M: Support notified C-172, and they confirmed latency is back to expected numbers. Customer asked for a writeup of the root cause and timeline. I'll draft and send after postmortem.

Alex G: Good job triaging. Notes for postmortem: include microbench CSV, kernel selection logs, the change that enabled flash by default, the probe heuristic implementation and why it timed out, and mitigation timeline (flag -> canary -> hotfix). Also include follow-ups: improve testing matrix for seq_len>512, per-tenant runtime flagging, and add alerts on kernel_probe_count spikes.

Rachel T: One more ask from Support — can we expose an API header `X-Redwood-Runtime-Flags: disable_flash_attention=1` for advanced customers to opt-out immediately? That would avoid routing work.

Priya S: We have the infrastructure for per-request runtime flags for internal testing; exposing it to customers needs an auth guard + logging. Put it in the postmortem wishlist; reasonable but not immediate.

Alex G: OK. Closing loop: hotfix rolled, customer happy, owners assigned. We'll assemble a short postmortem and hang in #postmortems and notify PMs. Thanks everyone. :tada:

Sofia M: filing INC-4123 and PM notify now.

Jamal R: uploading bench CSV + kernel traces to s3://redwood-perf/incidents/INC-4123/

Alex G: Marking this thread resolved for now. If you see any recurrence ping me directly.
